cases.why: `exact` elaborates a proof TERM (application, anonymous constructor, universal instantiation), not only a hypothesis name.
`cases h with a b` binds the components under the proof's own names; the arity is checked against the shape and a chosen exists-witness must be genuinely fresh.
`induction n` names its target. An inner binder is GENERALIZED — the goal's forall prefix is reordered and bridged back by UniversalIntro/UniversalInst alone, so no new rule and no new axiom.
The constructor scheme is read off the in-scope induction premises instead of being hard-wired to Peano, so a list goal splits on ENil/ECons and routes to the already-certified induction_over.
`rewrite` accepts a forall-quantified equation, instantiates it at the FIRST match, and certifies through a UniversalInstTerm chain. Substitution is capture-avoiding throughout.
`simp only [h]` builds the rule set from exactly the named hypotheses; an unknown name or one that does not orient is an error.

Blocked outside this bunch: needs `decide.rs`. The `Not` arm needs a refutation channel (`of_decide_eq_false`), which decide.rs's own comment already flags as a follow-up, and the bignum half needs `eval_int` to leave i64.
`ring` is a tactic-script atom over the same commutative-ring oracle ArithDecision certifies through, consulted at tactic time so a non-identity is declined rather than blown up at the trust door.

Blocked outside this bunch: `InferenceRule::ExistentialIntro` (lib.rs) carries its witness as a `String` that the certifier resolves as a Var or a Global, so a compound witness has no faithful image. Needs the `UniversalInst`/`UniversalInstTerm` treatment. The script surface, the `+` lexer and the variable-vs-constant resolution all landed; `exists` now DECLINES a compound witness rather than handing back a derivation the kernel refuses.
`<;>` applies its right-hand tactic to exactly the goals the left hand produced — told apart by node index, since those only ever grow.

Blocked outside this bunch: the script is `auto`, i.e. `engine.rs`. Composing `=` with `<` with `<=` also has no rule to compose with — the order fragment has LeTrans and LtSuccLe but no `le_succ_lt`, so `a<c<=d |- a<d` is not expressible in the current rule set at all.
`by_contra h` is a STEP: it binds the negation and leaves the absurdity, certified as ClassicalReductio so the axiom footprint still records that it went classical.

Blocked outside this bunch: `InferenceRule::Rewrite` (lib.rs) carries no occurrence index and `certifier.rs::build_equality_predicate` abstracts EVERY occurrence of the term, so a first-occurrence rewrite cannot certify. The test's own doc comment names this.
`focus` / `next` focus one goal and make it an ERROR for the block to leave it open; a failed block commits nothing.
`have h from <term>` adds a locally-proved hypothesis carrying its own derivation, so each use emits that proof — no lifted theorem, and a statement mentioning an intro-bound variable works.
`refine <term>` spawns one proof-STATE goal per `?` hole, in source order, never a kernel Term::Hole (which types_equal matches against anything).

An admitted proof is not a proof, and LOGOS has no encoding of one that is not worse than refusing. `add_declaration("sorryAx", T)` resolves through `get_global` exactly like `dne` or `le_trans`, and with no attribute system and no `#print axioms` analogue it leaves no marker at all — Prop becomes inhabited by fiat and the certificate still reads PRELUDE_VERSION "logos-coc-1". `Term::Hole` is worse: `types_equal` matches it against anything, so the gap does not even localise to one type. Emitting a `verified == false` artefact merely defers the "this is not a proof" call to whoever reads the report. Admitting is in scope only once axiom-closure tracking exists to make the poisoning of the whole downstream cone visible; until then a loud refusal is strictly the better answer, and it is what we do today.
